name: bluewater-01-worst-plumber-simple
lines: The worst plumber in your town is getting your calls.
And it costs the best one thirty seven thousand dollars a year.
Give me five minutes.
I will show you how he does it. And how you can do it too.
Meet Mike. He is an example, not a real client.
Fifteen years fixing pipes. He does it right the first time.
And this is Kyle. Two years in.
His fixes leak. A lot.
So who gets more calls?
Kyle. And it is not even close.
Here is why. It is nine at night. A pipe bursts in Sara's kitchen.
She grabs her phone and types three words. Plumber near me.
A few names pop up. Kyle is at the top.
Mike? Mike is nowhere.
Sara does not know Mike is better. How could she?
So she calls the first name she sees.
This happens to Mike about three times a week.
That is one hundred and fifty six calls a year.
Say three in ten would have hired him. That is forty seven jobs.
Now times that by eight hundred dollars a job.
Thirty seven thousand, four hundred and forty dollars. Gone.
To a guy who fixes pipes with duct tape.
Mike is not losing because he is worse.
He is losing because nobody can find him.
Kyle did three small things. None of them take skill.
And you can do all three this week.
But first. How does Google pick those names?
Google says it comes down to three things.
One. Relevance. Do you match what she typed?
Two. Distance. How close are you to her?
Three. Prominence. How well known are you? That includes your reviews.
Say Sara types water heater repair.
If your profile never says water heater, Google shows her someone who does.
You cannot move your shop closer to every customer.
But the other two? Those are all yours.
Thing one. Finish your Google profile.
Google only knows what your profile tells it.
Mike's profile is half empty. So Google has nothing to work with.
A finished profile has five things.
The right category. Plumber. Not contractor.
Every service, by name. Water heaters. Drains. Leaks.
Your real hours. Yes, the emergency ones too.
The area you really serve.
And real photos. Your work. Your van. Your face.
Here is how. Search your own business name on Google while you are signed in.
Tap edit profile. Then fill in every empty box. Every single one.
In the description, say what you do and where, in plain words. Like this. We fix leaks, drains and water heaters in Burnaby.
That is about twenty minutes of typing. And you only do it once.
That was the easy one.
The next one is where Kyle really beat Mike.
Thing two. Ask every customer for a review.
Mike has twelve reviews. All five stars.
Kyle has one hundred and eighty seven. Some are bad.
And Kyle still looks like the safer pick. More people have spoken.
Mike's customers love him.
He just never asks.
So ask. At the door. When the job is done and they are smiling.
Say this. If you were happy with the work, a quick Google review really helps a small business like mine.
I will text you the link right now.
Your review link lives inside your profile. Tap read reviews. Then get more reviews.
Copy that link and save it in your phone.
Then send that text before you leave the driveway.
Here are two rules.
Reply to every review. Good and bad.
And never pay for one. No cash. No discounts. Google does not allow it.
Got a bad one? Do not hide.
Reply within a day. Say sorry. Offer to fix it.
The next customer is watching how you handle it.
Now the fun part. Two jobs a day. You ask every time. One in four says yes.
That is one hundred and thirty new reviews in one year.
That is two down.
The last one hurts the most.
Thing three. Answer your phone.
A new customer calls at four past nine.
Mike is under a sink. It rings out.
She does not leave a message. She calls the next name.
Every call you miss is a call Kyle answers.
Here are three fixes.
One. Call back within five minutes. Every time.
Two. Set up a text that sends itself when you miss a call.
Three. When you really cannot pick up, let someone else answer.
The text can be this simple. Sorry I missed you. I am on a job. I will call you back in ten minutes.
Then do exactly that.
Three things that will get you in trouble.
Do not stuff extra words into your business name. Use your real name.
Do not list an address you do not work from.
And do not buy reviews.
Google can suspend your profile for any of these. Then nobody finds you at all.
Now test yourself. Do it tonight.
Open a private window. Search your trade and your town.
Not in the first few names? You just watched your own calls go to someone else.
Here is the good news. None of this takes talent. And Mike already has the talent.
It takes one hour.
Twenty minutes to finish the profile.
Twenty minutes to add real photos.
Twenty minutes to text your last ten customers and ask for a review.
Be patient. This moves in weeks, not days.
And nobody can promise you the top spot.
Mike's number was thirty seven thousand dollars. Yours is different. So work it out.
Calls you miss in a week. Times fifty two.
Times how many become jobs. Times what a job pays.
So. Finish the profile. Ask for the review. Answer the phone.
That is all of it. If you want a hand, we are Bluewater Co.
He is not cheaper. He is not better. He is just easier to find.
Here is the part that stings. Mike has been doing this thirteen years longer than Kyle.
Do not rush the category. Pick the one closest to your main job. Google lets you add more after.
Add photos of real jobs. Before and after. Your van outside a real house. No stock pictures.
The best time to ask is the moment they say thank you.
Check your voicemail greeting too. Say your name, your trade and when you will call back.
And if you only do one thing tonight, search your own trade and your town.
Mike did all three in one week. It cost him nothing but an hour.
